newsitem.title: USA: Pop star Jackson marries for the second time.
newsitem.headline: Pop star Jackson marries for the second time.

text.p: Pop superstar Michael Jackson married the woman who is carrying his child in a private ceremony in Sydney, Australia, his publicist said on Thursday.

Christine Holevas, Jackson's spokeswoman, said the singer exchanged wedding vows with Debbie Rowe, a 37-year-old nurse, while on the Australian leg of his HIStory world tour. "They are married. All I know is that it happened," Holevas said.
"Please respect our privacy and let us enjoy this wonderful and exciting time," Jackson told reporters in a written statement.

The wedding took place only 10 days after Jackson announced that Rowe, a longtime friend, was pregnant and was due to give birth in early 1997. Jackson denied news reports that Rowe had been artificially inseminated and paid $500,000 to carry his child.
"I am thrilled that I will soon be a father and am looking forward with great anticipation to having this child," Jackson said when the pregnancy was announced.

This is his second marriage. In January, Lisa Marie Presley, daughter of late rock-'n'-roll legend Elvis Presley, filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences 20 months after they were married in secret in the Dominican Republic.

Some Hollywood insiders had speculated that Jackson's first marriage was little more than a publicity stunt to deflect media attention over allegations that Jackson sexually molested a young boy. Jackson vehemently denied the charges and Los Angeles prosecutors decided not to file criminal charges in late 1994 after the boy refused to cooperate.
That came after Jackson agreed in January 1994 to pay the boy a multi-million settlement in return for dropping a civil lawsuit against the singer.

Rowe has reportedly been divorced for eight years from her first husband and lives in an apartment in the Los Angeles suburb of Van Nuys. She is said to have met Jackson 15 years ago while working for a doctor who was treating the entertainer for a rare skin condition.
According to news reports, Rowe was expected to move into Jackson's Neverland estate near Santa Barbara, California, when she returns home.

Jackson, dubbed the "King of Pop," was in Australia on the first leg of his HIStory world tour to promote his latest album, a compilation of new songs and some of his best known hits. The album contained Jackson's first new songs since his career was sidetracked by the sexual molestation scandal.
While the album debuted at the top of the Billboard chart it failed to generate the phenomenal sales of Jackson's previous efforts and quickly dropped out of the top 10.

His tour of Asia in October sparked controversy wherever it went. In Malaysia one concert was abruptly cancelled by authorities over concerns the show could have undesirable effects on youth, and civic and religious groups in South Korea failed to have a concert banned when the Ministry of Culture said Jackson could perform provided he refrained from making "obscene or vulgar gestures and remarks."
